catalyst_text: Announced positive interim extension results in NT1
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported a planned interim analysis from an ongoing long-term extension study in adults with narcolepsy type 1. Sustained improvements at week 24 were observed on MWT and ESS with normative wakefulness, reductions in cataplexy, and no serious TEAEs, supporting durable efficacy and tolerability.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alkermes plc (NASDAQ:ALKS) today announced results from a planned interim analysis of the ongoing long-term extension (LTE) study evaluating alixorexton in adults with narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) and narcolepsy type 2 (NT2). This ongoing open-label extension study is designed to evaluate the long-term safety, tolerability and durability of treatment effect of alixorexton. This interim analysis reflects safety and tolerability data as of the 2026-05-12 data cutoff and efficacy measures collected at week 24 of the LTE for participants who enrolled in the LTE after completing Vibrance-1 (NT1) or Vibrance-2 (NT2), reflecting treatment with alixorexton for up to nine months. All alixorexton dose groups for NT1 achieved normative wakefulness on the MWT (mean sleep latency (MSL) ≥20 minutes) at week 24 of the LTE, with a mean observed MSL of approximately 29 minutes across LTE participants. Improvements in ESS from baseline were sustained in the normal range (a score of ≤10) for all doses tested throughout the LTE, with a mean observed ESS of 7.5 at week 24 across LTE participants. No serious treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were reported.

catalyst_text: Announced positive interim extension results in NT2
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported a planned interim analysis from an ongoing long-term extension study in adults with narcolepsy type 2. At week 24, further improvements in MWT (mean MSL ~18 minutes) and normal-range ESS at higher doses were sustained, with no serious TEAEs, indicating durable benefit and tolerability.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alkermes plc (NASDAQ:ALKS) today announced results from a planned interim analysis of the ongoing long-term extension (LTE) study evaluating alixorexton in adults with narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) and narcolepsy type 2 (NT2). This interim analysis reflects safety and tolerability data as of the 2026-05-12 data cutoff and efficacy measures collected at week 24 of the LTE for participants who enrolled in the LTE after completing Vibrance-1 (NT1) or Vibrance-2 (NT2), reflecting treatment with alixorexton for up to nine months. All alixorexton dose groups for NT2 demonstrated further improvement on the MWT at week 24 of the LTE, with mean observed MSL of approximately 18 minutes across LTE participants. Improvements in ESS were sustained in the normal range (a score of ≤10) for the 14 mg and 18 mg dose groups throughout the LTE. No serious TEAEs were reported. Most TEAEs were mild to moderate in severity.

catalyst_text: Presented positive phase 2 data at APSS meeting
detailed_catalyst_text: Detailed results from the phase 2 Vibrance-2 study in narcolepsy type 2 met dual primary endpoints on MWT and ESS versus placebo. Improvements in wakefulness, fatigue, and cognition were sustained through week 13 and were presented at the APSS SLEEP meeting. These data support the efficacy of an orexin 2 receptor agonist in NT2 and inform advancement of development.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alkermes plc (NASDAQ:ALKS) today announced detailed positive results from the Vibrance-2 phase 2 dose-ranging study evaluating alixorexton in patients with narcolepsy type 2 (NT2). Once-daily alixorexton met the study's dual primary endpoints, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements from baseline compared to placebo on the Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (MWT) and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) at week eight in adults with NT2 (n=93). Results from Vibrance-2 were presented in an oral presentation at the 40th annual meeting of the Associated Professional Sleep Societies (APSS), taking place 2026-06-14 to 2026-06-17 in Baltimore, MD. Patient-reported improvements in wakefulness were sustained through the five-week open-label extension period.

catalyst_text: Initiated phase 3 program in narcolepsy type 1
detailed_catalyst_text: A global phase 3 program has been initiated to evaluate once-daily and split-dose regimens in narcolepsy type 1. This marks progression of the program into late-stage clinical testing following supportive phase 2 outcomes. It reflects advancement toward potential registrational studies in this indication.
catalyst_text_evidence: Based on the positive results demonstrated by alixorexton in the phase 2 Vibrance Studies, Alkermes has initiated a global phase 3 program evaluating once-daily and split dose regimens of alixorexton in patients with NT1 and NT2.

catalyst_text: Announced positive phase 3 topline results in idiopathic hypersomnia
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results were reported from the randomized withdrawal phase 3 REVITALYZ study in adults with idiopathic hypersomnia, where the primary endpoint (ESS) and key secondary endpoints (PGI-C and IHSS) were met with highly significant differences versus placebo. The data support clinical efficacy of a once-nightly extended-release sodium oxybate in IH, a population with limited approved options. Safety findings were consistent with prior experience, with no new signals observed.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alkermes plc (NASDAQ:ALKS) today announced positive topline results from the REVITALYZ℠ double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal, multicenter phase 3 study evaluating the investigational use of LUMRYZ® (sodium oxybate) extended-release oral suspension in adults with idiopathic hypersomnia (IH). LUMRYZ met the study's primary endpoint, demonstrating statistically significant improvements in excessive daytime sleepiness compared to placebo as measured by the change in Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS)1 score (p<0.0001). From the end of the stable dose period to the end of the double-blind randomized withdrawal period, participants randomized to placebo had statistically significant worsening in ESS (p<0.0001), PGI-C (p<0.0001), and IHSS (p<0.0001) compared with participants randomized to continue treatment with LUMRYZ. The safety profile of LUMRYZ in the REVITALYZ study was generally consistent with previously observed safety data associated with LUMRYZ, with no new safety signals observed in this population.

catalyst_text: Reported positive phase 2 open label extension data
detailed_catalyst_text: New phase 2 Vibrance-1 results in narcolepsy type 1 included seven-week open-label extension findings showing sustained improvements in patient-reported disease severity, cognitive functioning, and fatigue from baseline. The treatment was generally well tolerated with no serious treatment-emergent adverse events, reinforcing durability of effect and safety signals observed to date.
catalyst_text_evidence: — Alixorexton Data From Seven-Week Open-Label Extension Period Demonstrated Sustained Improvements in Patient-Reported Disease Severity, Cognitive Functioning and Fatigue— Alixorexton was generally well tolerated at All Doses Tested — Vibrance-1, a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind phase 2 study conducted in 92 patients with NT1, demonstrated clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvements from baseline compared to placebo in wakefulness, cognition, and fatigue. The new data demonstrate clinically meaningful improvements from pre-treatment baseline on established measures evaluating excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy, as well as participant-reported outcomes, including narcolepsy symptom severity, cognitive functioning and fatigue in patients with NT1 through the seven-week open-label extension. Alixorexton was generally well tolerated across all doses tested throughout the six-week, RDBT period and the seven-week open-label extension period. No serious treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were reported.
